knowledge:
- key_parameters: Data=A SummarizedExperiment, SingleCellExperiment, or matrix of raw counts (rows: genes, columns: cells) ;; BETA_vec=A vector of cell-specific capture efficiencies (probabilities) of length equal to the number of cells. If NULL, estimated to be total counts normalized to 6% ;; Conditions=If specified, prior parameters are estimated locally within each group of cells ("LL" procedure). Otherwise, a global "GG" procedure is used ;; Prior_type=Can be set to "GG" to estimate prior parameters globally across all cells even if Conditions is specified ;; mode_version=Logical; if TRUE, returns a 2D matrix of normalized data representing the MAP (mode) of the posterior ;; mean_version=Logical; if TRUE, returns a 2D matrix of normalized data representing the mean of the posterior ;; S=Number of samples to draw from the posterior distribution when generating a 3D array (used when mode_version and mean_version are FALSE) ;; UMI_sffl=A scaling factor for non-UMI datasets; raw data is divided by this number and rounded before applying bayNorm ;; PRIORS=Input for bayNorm_sup containing previously estimated prior parameters (from bayNorm_output$PRIORS) ;; input_params=Input for bayNorm_sup containing the parameters used in the original bayNorm run
- alternatives: scran=Mentioned as an alternative method for estimating scaling factors, which can then be normalized to the mean capture efficiency using BetaFun or manual scaling ;; SCnorm=Mentioned in the context of downstream differential expression (DE) analysis using the SCnorm_runMAST or SCnorm_runMAST3 functions
- when_to_use: Appropriate for normalizing scRNA-seq datasets (especially UMI-based, but also non-UMI with scaling) to correct for cell-to-cell variation in capture efficiency and sequencing depth while preserving biological variability for downstream analyses like differential expression detection
- pitfalls: Using the Method of Moments (MME) alone for estimating the size parameter (phi) introduces systematic bias; bayNorm defaults to a combined method that adjusts MME estimates using a linear regression with BB (marginal likelihood) estimates ;; Optimizing the marginal distribution with respect to both mu and phi (2D optimization) is computationally intensive; the combined method is preferred for efficiency ;; For non-UMI datasets, failing to specify UMI_sffl may lead to dropout vs. mean expression plots that do not resemble UMI datasets, violating model assumptions

workflows.name: standard_baynorm_normalization
workflows.intent: Estimate cell-specific capture efficiencies and perform Bayesian normalization on scRNA-seq count data to generate 3D posterior samples or 2D MAP/mean matrices.
input: rse (SummarizedExperiment or SingleCellExperiment object containing raw scRNA-seq counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Estimate cell-specific capture efficiencies using BetaFun ;; 2. Run bayNorm to perform normalization and generate a 3D array of posterior samples
workflows.code:
BETA_est<-BetaFun(Data=rse,MeanBETA=0.06)
bayNorm_3D<-bayNorm(
    Data=rse,
    BETA_vec = NULL,
    mode_version=FALSE,
    mean_version = FALSE,S=20
    ,verbose =FALSE,
    parallel = TRUE)

workflows.name: baynorm_supplementary_generation
workflows.intent: Generate alternative 2D normalized matrices (MAP or mean of posterior) using pre-existing prior parameters estimated from a previous bayNorm run.
input: rse (SummarizedExperiment or SingleCellExperiment object containing raw scRNA-seq counts)
bayNorm_3D (List output from a previous bayNorm run containing estimated priors and input parameters)
workflows.stages: 1. Run bayNorm_sup with mode_version=TRUE to generate a 2D MAP matrix ;; 2. Run bayNorm_sup with mean_version=TRUE to generate a 2D posterior mean matrix
workflows.code:
bayNorm_2D<-bayNorm_sup(
    Data=rse,
    PRIORS=bayNorm_3D$PRIORS,
    input_params=bayNorm_3D$input_params,
    mode_version=TRUE,
    mean_version = FALSE,
    verbose =FALSE)
bayNorm_2D<-bayNorm_sup(
    Data=rse,
    PRIORS=bayNorm_3D$PRIORS,
    input_params=bayNorm_3D$input_params,
    mode_version=FALSE,
    mean_version = TRUE,
    verbose =FALSE)
